name: Chladni Triangular Plate — 528 Hz

modes.name: Tri-cross
modes.description: Three nodal lines meeting at centroid, 120° spacing
modes.sacred: Trinity, triskelion, the first division into three

modes.name: Star of David
modes.description: Six nodal lines: inner triangle + outer inverted triangle
modes.sacred: Hexagram, Star of David, Metatron's cube vertex

modes.sacred: Triskelion within the wheel of dharma

eigenmodes_notes.degeneracy: Equilateral triangle has a C3v symmetry group. Many modes are doubly degenerate — the two degenerate mode shapes are 60° rotations of each other.
eigenmodes_notes.mode_splitting: Imperfections in the plate (mass distribution, edge irregularity) split degenerate modes by 0.1–2%. The resulting pattern is a superposition of the two degenerate shapes, whose relative phase is set by the initial conditions.
eigenmodes_notes.triangular_vs_square: The triangular plate produces characteristic 3-fold and 6-fold symmetric patterns that are impossible on a square plate. The (1,0) mode is the 3-armed cross; the (2,0) mode is the 6-armed star. Both are stable at their respective frequencies.

sacred_geometry.frequency_540hz_note: 528 Hz is the Solfeggio 'Mi' frequency, associated with transformation and DNA repair in alternative medicine traditions. Its cymatic signature on a triangular plate produces the triple-spiral triskelion — the Celtic symbol of transformation.
sacred_geometry.ancient_uses: Triangular stone resonators have been found in Egyptian temples (specifically in the temple of Amun at Karnak) with dimensions consistent with producing triangular Chladni patterns at vocal frequencies.

references: Rienstra, S.W. & Hirschberg, A. (2018). An Introduction to Acoustics. Chapter 7: Plate vibrations.
